title: Dominic and the Cipher
premise: Marguerite Voss, archivist of Saint-Aubin's cathedral, receives two letters in the same hand: one confessing to a murder committed twenty years ago inside the locked crypt, the other promising a full account if she can find 'the witness who never died.' Following the cipher hidden in the cathedral's own cataloguing system, Marguerite discovers the witness is Father Anselme, the beloved priest who supposedly died abroad — alive, hidden, and guarding proof that the town's founding families buried a girl to protect their heir. As Marguerite falls for Dominic Ferreol, the confessor's son sent to silence the archive, love and duty collide: he was raised to destroy the evidence she has sworn to keep. In the crypt's final reckoning, Dominic chooses truth over inheritance, the founding families fall, and Marguerite opens the sealed crypt at last — filing the town's darkest secret where it belongs.
about_author: E. M. Galloway is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade among ledgers, seals, and locked drawers before turning to fiction. Galloway writes mysteries about the quiet violence of small towns and the people paid to remember what others prefer forgotten.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: Marguerite Voss, cataloguing on a rainy evening in the cathedral archive, opens two letters postmarked the same day: a confession to a murder in the locked crypt, and a taunting promise of more. Her POV establishes her ordered world cracking. Emotional beat: unease dressed as curiosity.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Secrets
chapters.summary: Marguerite searches her own files for the murder year and finds pages razored out — by someone with archival access. She suspects her assistant, old Berthe, who goes silent. POV: Marguerite. Beat: the horror that the rot is inside her trusted system.

chapters.title: The Son Returns
chapters.summary: Dominic Ferreol arrives claiming to research his late father's parish record; his charm disarms Marguerite even as he asks oddly precise questions about the crypt. His POV reveals his real errand: find and destroy the confession. Beat: attraction shadowed by deception.

chapters.title: What the Crypt Keeps
chapters.summary: Marguerite gives Dominic the official tour but refuses him the crypt key, noting his flinch at the name Vernet — the murdered girl's family. Interleaved: a 20-year-old ledger fragment naming four founding families. Beat: first solid thread of conspiracy.

chapters.title: Berthe's Silence
chapters.summary: Marguerite confronts Berthe, who admits only that 'we all agreed to forget,' then suffers a fall on the archive stairs that may not be accidental. Marguerite's POV, fear hardening into resolve. Beat: the stakes turn physical.

chapters.title: Cipher in the Catalogue
chapters.summary: Deciphering shelf-mark anomalies Berthe left behind, Marguerite finds a pattern pointing to Father Anselme — the priest whose death abroad closed the case. Dominic, watching her work, realizes she is ahead of him. Dual tension: he must warn his handlers or protect her. Beat: reluctant alliance forms.

chapters.title: The Grave That Is Empty
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Dominic visit Anselme's memorial plot; the coffin holds stones. A groundskeeper mentions an old man who buys candles every month. Marguerite's POV, exhilaration and dread. Beat: the dead witness is alive.

chapters.title: Candlelight at Vespers
chapters.summary: Marguerite tails the candle-buyer to a shuttered convent outside town; Dominic follows her, torn between duty and something warmer. They lose the figure but find a fresh cipher matching the letters' hand. Beat: they are being led — or tested.

chapters.title: Dominic's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV flashback: his father's deathbed instruction, the family fortune built on the Vernet girl's disappearance, and his uncle Armand's cold expectation that he finish the job. Beat: the cost of obedience made personal.

chapters.title: The Second Letter Arrives
chapters.summary: A third letter reaches Marguerite directly: 'You are closer than my killers know. Trust no Ferreol.' She must weigh it against the man who has begun to feel like home. Marguerite's POV. Beat: love against duty, first fracture.

chapters.title: Armand Ferreol's Dinner Table
chapters.summary: Armand invites Marguerite to the family estate, offering her a funded restoration of the archive if she surrenders 'irregular documents.' She declines; his courtesy curdles. Dominic witnesses, complicit. Beat: power shows its velvet glove.

chapters.title: Berthe Speaks at Last
chapters.summary: Recovering in hospital, Berthe confesses her role: she helped file the girl's death as an accident and has been passing ciphers to Anselme for years. Marguerite's POV, grief for her mentor. Beat: guilt is contagious; everyone kept the secret.

chapters.title: The Convent Opens
chapters.summary: Using Berthe's final cipher, Marguerite and Dominic breach the convent and meet Father Anselme — aged, unrepentant about hiding, armed with the original coroner's report proving murder. Beat: the witness found; the truth heavier than imagined.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Anselme recounts the night in the crypt: young Dominic's father struck Céleste Vernet, and four families agreed to seal it. He hid because the police commissioner was a cousin. Dominic hears his father named as killer. Beat: shattering of filial loyalty.

chapters.title: The Betrayal
chapters.summary: Armand's men raid the convent; Anselme is taken, the report seemingly burned. Marguerite learns Dominic told his uncle where they'd be — or did he? His POV: he gave a false address, but someone followed them. Beat: trust broken by circumstance, not choice.

chapters.title: Ashes and Microfilm
chapters.summary: Marguerite discovers Berthe's true legacy: decades ago she microfilmed the entire crypt archive and hid the reels in plain sight, catalogued as hymnals. Marguerite's POV, grim triumph. Beat: the archivist's revenge — memory outlasts fire.

chapters.title: What Dominic Must Choose
chapters.summary: Armand offers Dominic full inheritance and Marguerite's safety in exchange for the reels. Dominic's POV at the crossroads: his name, his money, his mother's grave on Ferreol land — versus a woman and a dead girl. Beat: the theme crystallized.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Armand forces the crypt open himself to destroy remaining evidence, trapping Marguerite inside during the confrontation. Cliffhanger: stone grinding, air thinning, Armand holding the only key. Beat: terror in the story's heart of darkness.

chapters.title: Dominic Descends
chapters.summary: Dominic defies his uncle, takes the spare key from the sacristy, and opens the crypt as oxygen runs low; the confrontation ends with Armand collapsing — not struck down, but undone when Anselme, freed, walks in alive. Beat: climax; love chosen over blood.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Anselme's testimony plus the microfilm reels go to an outside magistrate; arrests ripple through the founding families. Marguerite testifies calmly, the archivist to the end. Beat: justice as procedure, satisfying and unsentimental.

chapters.title: Filing the Dead
chapters.summary: Marguerite formally catalogs Céleste Vernet's file, gives her a nameplate in the archive, and visits her restored grave with Dominic. Quiet grief and tenderness. Beat: memory honored; mourning given its proper shelf.

chapters.title: The Unlocked Door
chapters.summary: A year later: the crypt is open to visitors, Marguerite and Dominic share a life between archive and town, and a new letter arrives — this time simply thanking her. She smiles, files it, and locks nothing. Final beat: secrets end where love begins.
